title: Temkin stable modification of a multipointed relative curve
statement: Let $S$ be an excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring] integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] scheme with generic point [def-sc-generic-point] $\eta$. Let $C\to S$ and $H\to S$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms of pure relative dimensions $1$ and $0$, respectively, and let $H\hookrightarrow C$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Assume that $C_\eta$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and that $H_\eta$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] over $\kappa(\eta)$; $H$ may be empty. Then there are an integral excellent Noetherian scheme $\widetilde S$, a proper dominant generically finite morphism $a:\widetilde S\to S$, and a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] projective-bundle modification $b:\widetilde C\to C\times_S\widetilde S$ which is an isomorphism over the generic fibre, together with a closed subscheme $\widetilde H\hookrightarrow\widetilde C$ and a morphism $d:\widetilde H\to H\times_S\widetilde S$ such that $b\circ(\widetilde H\hookrightarrow\widetilde C)=(H\times_S\widetilde S\hookrightarrow C\times_S\widetilde S)\circ d$, the generic fibre of $d$ over $\widetilde S$ is an isomorphism, and $\widetilde C\to\widetilde S$ is flat and finitely presented of pure relative dimension $1$ and every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, while $\widetilde H\to\widetilde S$ is etale and $\widetilde H$ is contained in the relative smooth locus. The pair $(\widetilde C,\widetilde H)$ remains of this same semistable multipointed form after every base change of $\widetilde S$. Here generically finite means finite over a dense open of the target, and projective-bundle modification means projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] and proper with an isomorphism over a schematically dense open of its target; the generic-fibre isomorphism clauses refer to the generic point of $\widetilde S$.

source.place: Exposé X, §3.2.2 and proof of Theorem 3.4, Step 3, printed pp. 158--160: the definition of a semistable multipointed relative curve and the invocation of Temkin 2010, Theorems 1.5 and 1.1. Temkin's projectivity theorem and paper are not archived in literature; the ILO statement is the local source. The marking map and its generic isomorphism are part of a modification of multipointed curves and of an eta-modification in Temkin §1.2; Theorem 1.5 and Theorem 1.1 were also read online at the source URL during the repair. That definition explicitly allows nonseparated curves.
